title: Progent: Programmable Privilege Control for LLM Agents
abstract: Progent is a programmable privilege control framework for LLM agents, providing fine-grained control over tool calls and adaptive policy updates to prevent security breaches.

sections.title: The Core Insight
sections.content: Imagine a personal assistant that can manage your emails, but also has access to your financial information. Progent is a framework that restricts an agent's tool calls to only those necessary for its tasks, preventing potential security breaches. This is crucial, as LLM agents face significant security risks when interacting with external environments.

sections.title: How It Works
sections.content: Progent enforces privilege control at the tool level, restricting agents to making only necessary tool calls. It features a domain-specific language for expressing fine-grained policies, flexible fallback actions, and dynamic policy updates. JSON is used to define and validate tool calls.

sections.title: Benchmark Results
sections.content: Progent reduces attack success rates to 0% while preserving agent utility and speed. On the AgentDojo benchmark, LLM-generated policies reduce the attack success rate from 39.9% to 1.0%, with a utility score of 76.3% compared to the original agent's 79.4%.

sections.title: Why This Matters
sections.content: Progent addresses the critical security challenges faced by LLM agents, including indirect prompt injection, knowledge poisoning, and malicious tools. Its programmable framework and adaptive policy updates enable precise security controls, preserving agent utility and preventing security breaches.

sections.title: Key Innovations
sections.content: Progent introduces a novel security framework for LLM agents, featuring a domain-specific language, flexible fallback actions, and dynamic policy updates. Its modular design enables seamless integration with existing agent frameworks, requiring minimal code modifications.

sections.title: Try It Yourself
sections.content: To get started with Progent, users can define their own security policies using the provided domain-specific language. Progent's flexible fallback mechanisms and dynamic policy updates enable adaptive security controls, making it an essential tool for securing LLM agents.
